entries.title: Articles split across pages are joined into one
entries.body: When you add a web article by its address and its first page links on to the rest, such as an abstract leading to chapter pages, the AI picks which of those links on the same site continue the piece, and the parts that load are joined into one article. Before, only that first page was added; a part that will not load is skipped, and finding every part is not guaranteed. Uploaded files, scholarly papers and PDFs are added as before.

entries.title: Sources can place a piece in its literature
entries.body: In Sources, the Investigate view has a 'Search the literature' button that looks through other published work and gathers what it finds under 'Where this piece sits': where the piece has been challenged or supported, what came since, and what it does not cite. Each finding quotes its source, takes you to the passage it concerns and can be asked about in chat, and short notes appear beside the article. Only on articles you added, with the Experimental features switch on your profile page turned on.

entries.title: Spideryarn has a new mark: a reading spider
entries.body: The old spider is replaced by a spider sitting reading, in the page header, the browser tab, home-screen icons and the picture shown when you share a link. Large images use a woolly version and small icons a simpler one, and the logo's little animation was redrawn to match.

entries.title: Save for Spideryarn recognises a PDF
entries.body: On a PDF open in the browser, the Save for Spideryarn bookmark saved the browser's viewer rather than the document; it now says the page is a PDF and asks you to download it and upload the file. It also leaves out the parts of a page that could run code. Add the bookmark again to get this.
